items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: Jazzmen, that he knew like the bunch that was there, Claude Jones and Baixier and the rest, didn't need much arrangement for them

ctx.x: Well, I guess they figured George Jellie, being the way he was, he came up there, you know. He knew more buzz than any of them and they didn't.

They knew something about it. There was a little episode also about that, you know. As soon as they, they made two sides, I don't know, a couple of sides first. And Jellie was the leader and he arranged the studio arrangements for them, as much as they needed. Jazzmen, that he knew like the bunch that was there, Claude Jones and Baixier and the rest, didn't need much arrangement for them, but Jellie arranged for them. And he, they came to him and said, all right Jellie, now sign us the copyrights and we'll go…
He's going to make somebody else a leader.
